issues: whether a generic manufacturer may rely on grounds of invalidity not set out in its original notice of allegation
whether a court may raise the adequacy of a notice of allegation on its own motion (sua sponte)

whether the patent's description, by attributing specific properties (low toxicity, longer duration, superior safety over prior drugs) to the compound, creates a promise that the disclosure must satisfy

whether inaccurate experimental data in the patent specification (misidentified rodent species, incorrect dosing and timing, extrapolated rather than measured toxicity figure) defeats sufficiency of disclosure or utility
whether a compound patent based solely on animal testing, where the compound was never administered to humans, meets the utility requirement
the legal standard and effect of a prohibition application under the Patented Medicines (Notice of Claim) Regulations
the scope and validity of a compound patent claim versus a composition-of-matter claim directed to a specific therapeutic use (senile dementia)
key_facts: abbreviated submission filed with the federal health regulator for a generic oral Alzheimer's-type dementia medication
notice of allegation served challenging a listed compound patent
brand company and foreign patent owner applied to court to block approval until patent expiry
patent filed in the late 1980s based only on animal testing; compound never tested in humans
patent claims both the compound itself and a composition for treating senile dementia

lab records revealed: test described as one rodent species' brain tissue was actually another species; dosing and timing in a learning-impairment study were misstated; a toxicity figure was an extrapolation, not a measured dose
patent text characterizes the compound as having low toxicity, longer duration, and superior safety over two older drugs
the accuracy-of-data argument was not in the original notice of allegation because lab records were not yet available
the judge raised adequacy of notice sua sponte at the hearing
causes_of_action: prohibition application to block regulatory approval of a generic drug
challenge to patent validity (sufficiency of disclosure, utility, promise of the patent)
candidate_statutes: Patented Medicines (Notice of Claim) Regulations, SOR/93-1337
Food and Drugs Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-27
search_terms: new ground invalidity not in notice
